body:
Gold is trading around $4,310 per ounce today, September 14, 2026, and that level shows up consistently across both platforms rather than in any daily move worth flagging. Kalshi's September 30 settle above $4,290.99 contract sits almost exactly at a coin-flip (48¢ bid/49¢ ask), which is what you'd expect with spot sitting just below that strike. The scanner found zero arbitrage opportunities this run — nothing crossed the fee-adjusted threshold on either side.

The more interesting story is context, not today's tape. Gold hit an all-time high near $5,589 on January 28, 2026, then corrected sharply — one recap put the pullback at over 21% from that peak, driven by large-scale risk asset liquidations, a hawkish shift in Fed expectations, and a stronger dollar. That volatility is visible in Polymarket's weekly touch contracts: Will Gold hit (LOW) $4,250 Week of September 14 is priced 72¢/74¢, while the corresponding $4,400 touch-high sits at 37¢/39¢ — genuine two-sided uncertainty, not mispricing, since these are did it touch at any point contracts rather than settle-at-expiry contracts like Kalshi's.

Worth remembering when comparing the two boards: Kalshi's gold contracts settle on the spot price at a fixed future timestamp, while most Polymarket gold markets pay out if the touch level is hit anytime during the window. That structural difference, not any pricing error, explains why superficially similar strikes carry different odds across platforms. No opportunities, quiet day, and the pricing looks like normal reaction to a still-jumpy market well off its January highs.
headline: Gold steady near $4,310 as no arbitrage found between Kalshi and Polymarket contracts
